fieldMarks: North America's largest rodent, 0.9–1.2 m including tail; most adults 17–32 kg
Broad, flat, black tail about 25 cm long and 15 cm wide
behavior: Slaps the tail on the water as a warning
Fells trees (on average hundreds a year, up to about 40 cm diameter) for food and building
Builds dams, lodges and bank dens; castor from glands near the tail is used for scent marking
Usually stays within about 0.8 km of its den; two-year-olds disperse
habitat: Permanent water of almost any kind, preferring low-gradient streams, ponds and small mud-bottomed lakes with dammable outlets; needs 0.6–0.9 m of water year-round.
range: Throughout North America except Arctic tundra, peninsular Florida and much of the desert Southwest.

lookalikes.name: Muskrat
lookalikes.howToTell: The muskrat is far smaller (0.9–1.8 kg) with a rat-like, side-flattened tail.

lookalikes.name: Nutria
lookalikes.howToTell: Nutria have a round, sparsely haired tail and white whiskers; beavers have a broad flat tail and fully webbed hind feet.
